news.title: Chelsea's Ultimate Goal of the Season: Group D vote
news.body_en: We have reached the final group in our search for Chelsea’s Ultimate Goal of the Season, with five more spectacular strikes competing for the last two places in the quarter-finals. Groups A, B and C have already put 15 previous winners up for the vote, and Group D completes our line-up with goals from Ashley Cole, Lewis Baker, Eden Hazard, Mateo Kovacic and Moises Caicedo. The five contenders cover 14 years of Chelsea history and include everything from brilliant close control inside the penalty area to extraordinary efforts from distance. There is also something unique about this group. Baker’s 2014 winner came for our Under-21s against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium, making it the only Goal of the Season winner in our 20-goal field which was not scored for the men’s first team. Alongside it are memorable goals at Stamford Bridge and Anfield, including another piece of Hazard magic - incredibly his third entry into this competition, with the previous two having both advanced already. The two goals which receive the most votes will progress to the quarter-finals, completing the eight-goal line-up for the next stage of our Ultimate Goal of the Season contest. You can watch all five Group D contenders below, relive each special moment and choose your favourite by voting on the Chelsea Official App, so make sure you have your say on which strikes deserve to progress. Cast your vote for Group D of our Ultimate Goal of the Season on the Chelsea Official App here Cole raced on to John Terry’s lofted pass, brought the ball under control superbly in the box, cut inside a sliding challenge and then used the outside of his left foot to dink past the keeper and find the far corner during our 7-2 victory over Sunderland. Baker produced an outrageous finish for our Under-21s at the Emirates Stadium, meeting a cross from Islam Feruz first time and improvising brilliantly with a spinning backheel which flew into the Arsenal net, leaving the keeper looking bewildered. Hazard settled a Carabao Cup tie at Anfield in trademark fashion, surging past Naby Keita, nutmegging Alberto Moreno and then firing an unstoppable finish across goal from a tight angle to complete a 2-1 comeback victory. The goal gets better with every rewatch. With the Blues two goals down at Stamford Bridge, Kovacic met a punched clearance from the goalkeeper with a magnificent first-time volley - while moving backwards - from outside the penalty area, sending the ball in off the post to spark our fightback to a 2-2 draw. Caicedo chose a remarkable way to score his first Chelsea goal, collecting a loose clearance just inside his own half before launching an inch-perfect effort over the retreating defence and into the empty net from the halfway line. news.title: Ultimate Goal of the Season | Group D
Internationals: Lavia landmark but Lacroix wins battle of the Blues
news.body_en: There was Chelsea representation on both sides of the pitch as France snatched a late winner away to Belgium in UEFA Nations League action on Monday night. For the first time in his senior international career, Romeo Lavia was named in the Belgium starting line-up, anchoring the midfield in a double pivot alongside Youri Tielemans. Lavia put in an energetic performance and impressed with his defensive contributions, including a goal-line clearance. For the visitors, Maxence Lacroix helped France to a second clean sheet away from home in the space of four days, with Les Bleus emerging triumphant courtesy of substitute Michael Olise’s 88th-minute winner. The only goal arrived shortly after Lavia was replaced, while Lacroix played the full game. Mike Penders was not involved due to injury. France’s next game is at home to Italy on Friday night, the same evening Belgium host Turkey. At youth level, Chelsea Academy attacker Heze Grimwade scored the winning goal for England Under-17s as they came from behind to beat Israel 2-1 in Germany. The Young Lions equalised with 20 minutes remaining and almost immediately went ahead when substitute Grimwade finished clinically. Josh Henry and Reggie Watson both started the game – the first in a four-nation tournament – with Henry completing the 90 minutes and Watson withdrawn after England went 2-1 ahead. They next play Venezuela on Thursday.

news.title: Analysis: How Chelsea turned the tide against Arsenal
news.body_en: A big crowd, a fantastic mosaic in the West Stand and plenty of pre-match hype meant that our London derby with Arsenal at Stamford Bridge was hotly anticipated. But for all the pre-match buzz, it was the visitors who had the lion's share of the play in the opening stages, hitting the woodwork twice. For a while, it looked like the Blues were in trouble. But some careful game management, a lot of hard graft and a clinical moment from Alyssa Thompson meant that we came away with three precious points. Here's a look at how we did it... After scoring early in our last two matches, the wins over Birmingham City and Austria Vienna, Chelsea struggled to get hold of the ball against Arsenal. Head coach Sonia Bompastor has often spoken about the advantages of scoring early, explaining that it can serve to kill the opposition's hope early on in a game. Yet Arsenal had 65 per cent possession in the first 15 minutes of Sunday's game, leading many to wonder why we were not able to show the same attacking prowess that we had done in the previous two matches. Of course, it's not easy to dominate a high-level opponent, and that fast start was never guaranteed. If the plan was to let Arsenal have the ball early on, then it was difficult to understand why that would be, especially when we were at home. Bompastor confirmed that Arsenal's early dominance was not part of her tactics. 'We didn't start the way we wanted to,' confirmed the head coach afterwards. 'Our game plan was different from what we did in the first 20 minutes. When we got that break, it was the opportunity for me to adjust and to remind the players what we wanted to do on the pitch. 'We were able to recover that ball, and after that, we capitalised on it. But as much as you tell the players before the game that's what you want, sometimes it doesn't go to plan, and you need to find a way for them to adjust.' Reversing such clear momentum is not an easy task, but that's what Bompastor helped her players to do, and in the first 15 minutes of the second half, we enjoyed 72 per cent of the ball. Lucy Bronze has proven that she thrives in high-pressure moments, and has even discussed how she can raise her level when it matters in previous interviews. A home game against rivals Arsenal was one of those occasions for the experienced defender, and a look at her numbers shows how she led by example while wearing the captain's armband. Bronze won five of her six attempted tackles, the most of any Chelsea player on the day. She also made two blocks, won three aerial duels and recovered the ball on five occasions. Not only content to carry out her defensive duties against a quality opponent, she made 16 passes in the final third of the pitch, created one chance and took a shot at goal. It was a trademark battling display from the 34-year-old, and one that certainly helped us secure the win on Sunday. Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter has been playing more minutes this season, and developing an increasingly effective partnership with Keira Walsh. But few would've expected the youngster to be named in the starting line-up against Arsenal, with games of this magnitude often reserved for players with more experience. Bompastor showed how highly she values the youngster by placing her in the XI to start against the Gunners, and explained afterwards why she did so. 'For her age, being able to be consistent in the way she's been performing is great,' said the head coach. 'Probably people were also looking forward to this game to see if, on this big occasion, she was able to repeat and sustain the performance, and she proved that today.' It's not only her own performances that have secured a place in the side for Potter. Her reliability in the deeper midfield slot is allowing Walsh to express her qualities more in attack, as Bompastor also explained. 'Keira is playing at that level because she has more freedom to go forward, because she has Lexi next to her. When Keira is at that level, she's the boss on the pitch.' The graphic above shows how many of Walsh's touches are outside of the centre circle. And when compared to Potter's touch map below, it's clear that the 20-year-old is covering that central area in place of Walsh, allowing her counterpart to make a difference in attack. It's something that Walsh herself spoke about after the Arsenal victory. 'Last year I sometimes let games pass by without having much impact, and that's something I've focused on this season,' said Walsh after the match. 'Having Lexi behind allows me to do that.' It was a tough job to stay high up the pitch against Arsenal, but someone had to do it. The average position graphic below demonstrates how Chelsea were much less positionally aggressive against the Gunners than we have been in other matches this season. Some of that can be put down to playing an opponent who can be extremely dangerous on the counter-attack, but as discussed earlier, much of it was down to those early minutes of domination from the visitors. Up top was Melvine Malard, holding the line, battling for possession and being ready for any out ball that might've come her way. Playing the central striker role isn't always glamorous, but our summer signing has shown she is willing to do the hard work for the team. Taking five shots, two of which were on target, she also completed all eight of her passes in the final third, while winning the ball back twice and completing both of her attempted tackles. This was a clear indication of Malard's value to the team even on a day when she wasn't on the scoresheet.

news.title: Training gallery: Back to work!
Katie McCabe on playing smart and 'riding the storms' against former club Arsenal
news.body_en: Katie McCabe knows only too well the strengths of her former side, and that was exactly why she was delighted to seal the win against Arsenal at Stamford Bridge on Sunday afternoon. The Ireland captain made the move across London in the summer in search of a fresh challenge after ten years with the Gunners. And while others talked at length about her return to face them for the first time since that exit, McCabe was focused exclusively on helping earn three points for Chelsea. ‘For me it was all about us and our preparation going into the game,’ she said. ‘Obviously, we know Arsenal pose a lot of threats, and they've got a lot of quality on the ball and around the box, but it was up to us to ride the storm a little bit in the first half. ‘But once we settled in, got control of the ball, we dominated in periods and Alyssa (Thompson) took our goal really well. ‘As I said, Arsenal are a fantastic footballing team, and they're going to dominate at times, but it's what we do without the ball and how we can control the spaces. ‘And in the first part of the first half, we did it really well. In the second half, they changed formation; they put on a lot of attackers, so they were chasing the game, and we needed to stick together and grind out the result. ‘We got up the pitch, kept the ball in the corner, and sometimes it's just about playing smart. We did that and picked up the three points.’ The Arsenal fans, tucked in the corner at the far side of the East Stand, made their feelings known whenever McCabe touched the ball. But for an experienced professional, the reception is an ordinary part of playing football and will not taint her memories of the past. ‘Having been with the club for so long, it's expected, especially going to a London rival,' she explained. 'But I have a lot of respect for the Arsenal fans. ‘We've been through a lot together, but for me, it was time for a new chapter in my career. I was really excited to come to Chelsea with the way Sonia wants to play and the quality we have in the team. ‘I'm delighted with the win, and that's most important.’ Keira Walsh had plenty of positive words to say about her Irish team-mate in her post-match interview, and McCabe duly returned those compliments with some praise of her own. ‘We absolutely controlled everything in the midfield, and credit to Keira as always,' McCabe smiled. ‘I've played against her for so long. We’ve known each other a long time. Back in the Man City, Arsenal days, which are what… ten years ago now? I always heard the English girls coming back from camp saying, "Oh, Keira's in the team, Keira's in the team," and what she offers. ‘But actually playing with her means when I give her the ball under pressure, she brings calmness and composure. She doesn't lose the ball. ‘I don't want to jinx her now, but you can't get the ball off her, and I think she's just always five steps ahead of everyone else with her vision. I like to play through the lines - Keira's always an option for me. I trust her in those tight spaces, and she can score, too!’

news.title: WSL Full Match: Chelsea Women vs Arsenal Women
Keira Walsh on 'outfighting' Arsenal and 'exceptional talent' Lexi Potter
news.body_en: Keira Walsh reflected on the victory over Arsenal after another standout individual performance and explained exactly what this Chelsea side has added to our game to make us more difficult to beat this season. We have kept a clean sheet in our last three matches and only conceded three goals in our opening seven games of the season in all competitions. And while this side has always possessed the technical skill to dominate matches, Walsh thinks the difference-maker this season has been the team’s work rate and willingness to fight for each other. ‘It’s great to win any game, even if it wasn't Arsenal,’ the midfielder explained. ‘But they're a top team, and it made it a little bit more special that it was a home derby. ‘It was difficult for us, but we controlled the game for large parts of it. Then at the end, when it came to managing the game a little bit – because they were throwing loads of attackers on – defending our box and keeping a clean sheet was really important. ‘It was probably the best we've built up [this season]. We were really comfortable on the ball when we had it, especially after the first 20 minutes. We really settled down and grew into the game. ‘Probably it would’ve been better to start the game a little bit quicker. Last season maybe Arsenal probably would've scored then and it could’ve been 2-0 or 3-0. That's probably the difference this year, and I think we've got both sides to our game now. ‘We can control the ball, and we are also a lot more difficult to beat,' added Walsh. 'We're really tight defending our box now. Obviously, we know we can play with the ball, but maybe we can outwork and outfight teams. That's been something else we’ve been doing as well, and that really helped. ‘We do it as a team rather than individuals, and this year, we know we've got each other's backs. We're working for each other. If a ball goes past me, I know Lex (Lexi Potter) is there clearing up. We all work together and that's probably been the most important so far this season.’ Walsh and Potter have formed quite the duo in midfield this season. Head coach Sonia Bompastor showed her faith in the young Chelsea Academy graduate by handing her a starting berth in the London derby alongside her vastly more experienced counterpart. There may be a mismatch in terms of minutes played, but as Walsh explained, Potter is fitting in perfectly in the first team and has a bright future ahead of her. ‘Lexi is really intelligent,’ Walsh said. ‘She makes me feel really comfortable when I'm playing next to her. The way she sees the game, there aren't many female players who understand it the way she does. ‘She's an exceptional talent, and she plays beyond her years. She's got a very calm head on her shoulders, and she's got a lot more to come, I think. She’s going to be an incredible player for Chelsea and England in the future.’ Walsh chose to single out another of her team-mates in her post-match comments, praising Katie McCabe for the contribution she has made to the side on and off the pitch since her summer transfer from cross-city rivals Arsenal. Another player may have shrunk under the pressure of facing her former side, especially in the face of a largely hostile reception from the contingent of visiting supporters at Stamford Bridge. Yet McCabe stood tall and delivered another outstanding performance in blue, and it didn't go unnoticed. 'I think Katie coming to us has added an extra edge, and her physicality and mentality really ramp it up,' said Walsh. 'Every time she does a little team talk, we play quite well, so hopefully that continues. She's fitted in really well. 'I'm not surprised she handled the atmosphere, to be honest. That's the sort of player she is. She works hard every day; she wants to win every single part of every training session. I think we needed that a little bit more last year, and she's definitely brought that. I’ve enjoyed every minute playing with her. 'She's really smart; she’s got a great left foot as well, so she's brought a massive part to our team. She's just so passionate about the game and you can really feel it when she's speaking. It gets the players going and definitely gets me going, so it’s great if she keeps doing it.'

news.title: Jamie Gittens withdraws from England Under-21 squad through injury
news.body_en: Jamie Gittens has withdrawn from the England Under-21 squad after picking up an injury in Friday night's game against Kazakhstan. The winger was forced off after 39 minutes during England's 4-2 win, in which his Chelsea team-mate Josh Acheampong scored. Divine Mukasa has been called up as a replacement by Lee Carsley, with the Young Lions knowing they can book their place in next summer's European Championships in Albania and Serbia when they play Slovakia on Friday evening.

news.title: WNL Cup report: Maidenhead United 0-1 Chelsea Women Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women's Under-18s secured top spot in our Women's National League Cup group with a 1-0 win away at Maidenhead United, with Stevie Sinclair grabbing a 90th-minute winner. The Blues, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women's League and cup competition, had 74 per cent of possession but found it difficult to create clear chances in the first half against Maidenhead's 5-4-1 low block. Sadie Gregory hit the post during that spell. Chelsea had 13 shots after the interval, six of them on target. Maidenhead goalkeeper Cherry Priesner made important saves to deny Chelsea N'Drin and Nelly Las before substitute Sinclair struck late on. First team players Lola Brown, Las, and Chloe Sarwie featured for Leanne Champ's side for the first time this season. Chelsea had most of the ball from the start but were limited to efforts from distance and half-chances as Maidenhead defended deep. The closest we came in the first half was on 20 minutes. The ball was worked out from the right-hand side of the box to Gregory, and the centre-back stepped in and struck a curling left-footed shot that hit the left post. Ten minutes later, Las picked out her fellow wing-back Sarwie at the back post, but Sarwie narrowly missed the target with a flying volley. The Blues had five shots in the first half, none of which were on target, and the game was goalless at half-time. Champ made three changes at the break, bringing on Rebekah Pierce, Tess Finn and Sinclair for Gregory, Keira Johnson and Jahmya Putman. Chelsea were more threatening after the restart. On 64 minutes, Elise Christian replaced Annie Boichat. A minute later, N'Drin looked set to score after a failed clearance, but Priesner grasped the ball before it crossed the line. The Maidenhead goalkeeper denied Chelsea again on 76 minutes. Captain Belle Sullivan (pictured top) won the ball back high up the pitch, and Finn laid it off to Las on the edge of the box. Las struck across goal, but Priesner stopped the shot before it could go in. The breakthrough came in the 90th minute. Sinclair won the first contact from a Maidenhead goal kick, and after a battle for the loose ball in midfield, it broke to Brown with space to drive forward. Brown played the ball out to Pierce, who took on her defender one-on-one before playing a reverse pass to Las on the top left corner of the box. Las drove into the area and picked out Sinclair on the penalty spot, and she curled a left-footed shot into the top corner. It was Sinclair's third goal in the WNL Cup this season and her eighth in all competitions. A draw would have been enough for Chelsea to top the group, but the win means we ,finish on nine points, ahead of Tier 3 side Swindon Town on six, Tier 4 side Maidenhead on three and Wycombe Wanderers on zero. Chelsea move into the WNL Cup knockout stages, which is where our run ended last season. We were the only academy side to progress from the groups last term, and this season the Blues will be looking for a competitive draw and the chance to go further than any academy side has before. After a ten-day break, Chelsea begin our PGA Cup campaign at home against West Ham United Women Under-21s in the preliminary qualification round on Wednesday 7 October. The Blues then start the PGA National Division One season on Wednesday 18 November. We qualified after topping the Southern phase and finishing with the best record across the North and South divisions. Chelsea (3-4-3): Victoria Rudz; Annie Boichat (Elise Christian 64), Gabi Storey, Sadie Gregory (Rebekah Pierce 45); Nelly Las, Belle Sullivan (c), Keira Johnson (Tess Finn 45), Chloe Sarwie; Chelsea N'Drin, Jahmya Putman (Stevie Sinclair 45), Lola Brown Unused subs: Freya Weeks, Amelia Fahey, Emelia Addison Scorers: Sinclair 90 Manager: Leanne Champ

news.title: Chelsea’s Ultimate Goal of the Season: Group C results
news.body_en: The results for Group C of our Ultimate Goal of the Season competition are in, and we can now reveal which two strikes have progressed to the quarter-final vote. In fact, it is a familiar pairing that have advanced, with Michael Essien and Eden Hazard repeating their Group A success to ensure they will each have two goals featuring in the last eight. Essien’s crashing volley against Barcelona in 2009 is joined by Hazard’s iconic solo effort scored against Arsenal in 2017 after a vote contested on the Chelsea Official App. They beat off competition from Goal of the Season winners scored by Ramires (2011), Olivier Giroud (2021) and Conor Gallagher (2023). The hunt for Chelsea’s Ultimate Goal of the Season continues tomorrow (Tuesday) as we open the polls for Group D, so you make sure you log back in to the Chelsea Official App to watch the contenders and cast your vote!

news.title: Forward voted Star of the Match against Arsenal!
news.body_en: Chelsea earned a memorable 1-0 win over rivals Arsenal at Stamford Bridge on Sunday and Blues fans have voted for their standout performer. Alyssa Thompson's emphatic strike on 38 minutes was the only goal of the game, and the Blues fans inside the stadium were treated to a thrilling encounter in which the entire Chelsea side played a role in securing the three points. Thompson has been voted as your Star of the Match, earning a 47 per cent share of the votes for her match-winning strike and all-round hardworking performance. Coming in second place with 29 per cent of the votes was Lucy Bronze for her battling display at the back,  while Keira Walsh took third position with 20 per cent of the overall tally for another superb display in the middle of the park.

news.title: WSL Highlights: Chelsea Women 1-0 Arsenal Women
Internationals: Neto assists Portugal to victory
news.body_en: Pedro Neto created a goal for his former Chelsea team-mate Joao Felix as Portugal recorded an impressive 2-1 win away to Norway in the UEFA Nations League on Sunday evening. Neto played 87 minutes in Oslo and set up the opener after dribbling down the left wing and intelligently laying the ball into the path of Joao Felix, located on the edge of the box. He took a touch and finished with aplomb. That 16th-minute goal was cancelled out by Erling Haaland early in the second half, but Goncalo Ramos restored Portugal’s lead soon after following an error by Orjan Nyland. Ramos then thought he had scored a second, but a lengthy VAR checked showed there had been an offside in the build-up. Norway pressed for a second equaliser late on during an entertaining encounter, but the Portuguese stood firm to make it two wins from two as they seek to defend the Nations League crown they won last summer. Neto was replaced by Bernardo Silva three minutes from time. Elsewhere at senior level, Jorrel Hato was an unused substitute as the Netherlands beat Serbia 2-1 in Belgrade. Earlier on Sunday, four Chelsea players featured for England Under-18s as they qualified for the semi-finals of the UEFA Friendship Cup with a 2-1 win over Egypt in Nyon. Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, who is spending the season on loan at Portsmouth, opened the scoring on the quarter-hour with a superb strike from 20 yards out. The winger carried a threat throughout the first half, forcing a good save from the opposition goalkeeper following another mazy run and flashing an angled drive inches wide of the far post. Gabriel Sambou and Jashayde Greenwood were introduced midway through the second half, while Calvin Diakite also entered the fray, with Kavuma-McQueen one of those to make way. Egypt levelled with 11 minutes left but the Young Lions were soon back in front and it was Greenwood who supplied the precise pass that set up Michael Mills of Newcastle to score the winning goal. England Under-18s next play on Wednesday 30 September against South Korea.

news.title: 'The fans gave the team the boost they needed'
Sonia Bompastor on Lauren James' fitness and being 'strong and together' after Arsenal win
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor explained why Lauren James was substituted after 60 minutes of our 1-0 win over Arsenal and reflected on how the Blues were able to pull together to secure the three points. After a strong start to the game from the visitors, the Blues wrestled back momentum, taking the lead through Alyssa Thompson's strike on 39 minutes. Yet there was plenty of work still to be done as both sides exchanged chances in the second half. Chelsea dug deep to secure the three points, spurred on by the Blues fans who made themselves heard in what was an electric atmosphere inside Stamford Bridge. After grinding out a 1-0 victory against Austria Vienna in midweek, we recorded another hard-fought win against our London rivals, and the head coach explained that the tenacity shown by her players so far this season is something that the team has been working hard on behind the scenes. 'The plan for us this season is mindset and mentality,' explained Bompastor. 'I've been talking a lot about being strong and being together. No matter what happens in the game, I always want to see a group of players, and also a team who is together in our high moments when we doing well, but also in the low moments. 'We came into this game well-prepared in terms of knowing we were going to have some moments in the game where we were probably not in control, especially in possession of the ball, because we knew how good Arsenal are at doing that. 'So we prepared the game for those moments. Even if we didn't have the ball, we knew exactly where we wanted to rotate the ball and where we wanted to leave some spaces, and I think we dealt with that really well. 'We were also really strong in terms of the mental aspect, but also physical aspects: winning the duels and defending the box. To not concede against an Arsenal side who are a strong team with great talent in the attacking line, midfield, the fullbacks...everywhere, it's a great result and performance.' The win against Arsenal was our fourth consecutive clean sheet in all competitions. The Blues have only conceded three times in seven matches this season: two in our first fixture against Real Sociedad, and once against Aston Villa at Stamford Bridge. The head coach is pleased with our defensive performances, and with another big test to come away at Lyon on Wednesday night, the head coach explained how she would reflect on what can be learned from the latest win. 'I'm pleased with the effort the players put on the pitch today,' she continued.  'From the beginning of the season, we didn't concede a lot of goals, which is great. I'm pleased with that. 'We still have some work to be done in those areas, and then we'll reflect on the game and take the learnings. But I think it was a strong performance today in terms of the out-of-possession work.' After missing last Wednesday's match against Austria Vienna, Lauren James returned to the starting line-up today, but was withdrawn after an hour. Bompastor gave an update on her condition and explained why she was substituted. 'We knew after LJ got a knock in training, we didn't want to take any risks because this game was coming,' she said. 'Sometimes what is difficult for a head coach is that every game is important because when you think about rotating and managing the squad, you need to make sure you mainly win the games. 'With the information from the medical team from the beginning, I knew we were going to prepare for LJ to start this game, and it was great news. Having 60 minutes was probably a good plan because she hadn't played for one week. 'She didn't stay home for a long time, but I think maybe she still couldn't work the way she would have liked to. So 60 minutes was good, and she brought a contribution to the game.'

Match gallery: Blues triumph in London derby!
Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Arsenal
news.body_en: A superb strike from Alyssa Thompson and a battling second-half display earned us a 1-0 victory over Arsenal at Stamford Bridge in the London derby on Sunday afternoon. This was undoubtedly a big occasion at the Bridge. The fans in the West Stand held their cards aloft to spell out the word 'Blues' ahead of kick-off, and both sets of fans raised their voices in support of their respective sides. The Gunners took control in the opening stages of the game, hitting the woodwork twice as they dominated possession. But we played patiently and gradually got ourselves back into the contest before an emphatic finish from Thompson put us 1-0 up before half-time, to the delight of the home supporters. The second half saw both teams exchange chances; however, we pulled together strongly and, helped by our fans, saw out the victory to take all three points against our rivals at the Bridge. Sonia Bompastor made four alterations to her starting line-up from the side that recorded a 1-0 win over Austria Vienna in midweek. Livia Peng, Sandy Baltimore, Veerle Buurman and Sjoeke Nusken made way for Hannah Hampton, Lucy Bronze, Lauren James and Lexi Potter. Bronze took the captain's armband for the afternoon, and a fit-again Aggie Beever-Jones was named on the bench. The visitors dominated possession in the opening 15 minutes, taking four shots on goal, but they failed to threaten Hampton with any real penetration or attempts on target. That was until Gunners captain Kim Little got a fraction in front of Buchanan on the right-hand side of the penalty area and pulled the trigger, striking the woodwork with her effort from a tight angle. Then came our first real chance of the game when Ellie Carpenter put in a dangerous ball on the right that Wieke Kaptein couldn't quite reach. The ball fell to Melvine Malard, but a crowd of Arsenal players prevented her getting any clean contact on a shot. Renee Slegers' side made a quick breakaway straight after that chance, and the ball fell to Mariona Caldentey in acres of space. Her shot crashed against the near post, but it looked like Hampton had it covered. From that point, the Blues slowly gained a foothold into the game, increasing our possession of the ball and looking much more assured. Just as it was looking like the teams would head into the break all square, a brilliant passage of play gave us the advantage. Arsenal attempted to play out from the back from a goal kick, and the Blues were alive with our press as Wieke Kaptein intercepted the ball, finding Carpenter. The Australian evaded a tackle before Malard laid it off to Keira Walsh, who took a shot from the edge of the penalty area. When goalkeeper Anneke Borbe could only parry, Thompson seized her opportunity to take hold of the ball and fired in with power from the left corner of the six-yard box. We could've even had two before the break. Carpenter played a long ball down the channel to Malard. The No. 9 sprinted into the box, forcing a save from Borbe and winning a Chelsea corner. The second half began with a looping cross into the box from James, and as Borbe spilt the ball, Malard was almost there to net the rebound, but the offside flag stopped any chance of us doubling our advantage. Hampton was called into action shortly afterwards to deny a shot from Lisa Baum, the England international getting down well to keep out a strike with plenty of power. Malard went close again just after the hour mark, receiving a pass from Bronze on the edge of the box before her shot rolled agonisingly wide of the far post. Both sides continued to have chances as substitute Nusken nearly scored with her first touch, beating Leah Williamson but seeing her chance extinguished by the onrushing Borbe. Up at the other end, Katie McCabe made a crucial block on a shot from Arsenal substitute Chloe Kelly. As the minutes ticked down towards full time, the tension was high inside Stamford Bridge. Steph Catley whipped in a corner, which was punched away by Hampton and hacked clear by Sandy Baltimore. Arsenal were determined to throw the kitchen sink at us in an attempt to snatch a late equaliser. The referee indicated there would be five minutes remaining and there was a gasp around Stamford Bridge. Carpenter then ran the length of the pitch to put a cross into the box, but in the end, there was no one to meet it. Yet this helped to ease the pressure on the Blues just a little, as we ran the clock down by keeping the ball down that right-hand flank, and ultimately saw out the win with complete professionalism. The win leaves us just two points behind Women's Super League leaders Manchester City, with an away league fixture against West Ham United to come next Sunday 4 October. We travel to Bompastor's former side Lyon as we take on the French champions in the league phase of the Women's Champions League on Wednesday evening. Chelsea: Hampton, Carpenter, Bronze (c), Buchanan, McCabe (Buurman 89), Walsh, Potter, Kaptein, Thompson (Baltimore 88), James (Nusken 67), Malard (Beever-Jones 79)Unused substitutes: Peng, Girma, Bjorn, Dragoni, HamanoScorers: Thompson 39Booked: McCabe 45, Bronze 45+3 Arsenal: Borbe, Fox, Williamson, Catley, Batlle (Cerci 81), Little (C), Stanway (Blackstenius 61), Cooney-Cross, Caldentey (Foord 61), Baum (Kelly 61), Russo Unused substitutes: Misa, Wubben-Moy, Smith, Reuteler, Holmberg Referee: Emily Heaslip

news.title: Millie | A CFCW film 🎥
Millie Bright's incredible Chelsea tenure celebrated in behind-the-scenes exclusive documentary
news.body_en: Millie, an exclusive documentary celebrating the storied career of our former captain, Millie Bright, is now streaming on the Chelsea Official app and website! Bright retired from football in April after 12 unforgettable years at Chelsea. With 314 appearances and a place in the side for all 20 major trophies won in our history, her legacy will continue far beyond her playing days. She is the first women's team player to be immortalised on the Shed Wall, while the sensory room at Stamford Bridge is now named in her honour to mark the work she has done off the pitch, which she will continue after being named a Chelsea Foundation trustee. The documentary goes behind the scenes at her family home in Killamarsh, talking to her grassroots coaches and the Bright family about how she began her football journey as a child. It is available to watch in full below. Bright recounts some of the most personal moments of her incredible Chelsea career, discusses her winning mentality and talks with honesty about the reasons behind her decision to retire from football. The former Blues captain's career trajectory ran parallel to the growth of women's football, and she saw firsthand how the popularity of the Women's Super League exploded after she was part of England's Women's European Championship-winning side in 2022. 'I went in as one person, came out as something completely different,' she told us when she announced her retirement. 'It was the most overwhelming situation I've ever been in. I just didn't know what to do with myself. I didn't leave the house for six days!' There's also a look inside her passion for helping others and inspiring the next generation of footballers, as one of the most experienced voices in the women's game. This is a chance for Blues fans to get to know the person who lies underneath all the trophies and the success, and what drove her to reach those heights. The full in-depth documentary is available to watch exclusively on the Chelsea Official App and website - just make sure you are signed in!

news.title: Chelsea's Ultimate Goal of the Season: Group C vote
news.body_en: The search for Chelsea’s Ultimate Goal of the Season moves on to Group C, with another five memorable strikes competing for your votes! Groups A and B have already brought together the first 10 winners in our 20-goal contest and now it is the turn of Michael Essien, Ramires and Eden Hazard, all for the second time in this competition, as well as Olivier Giroud and Conor Gallagher. This group stretches from 2009 to 2023 and includes goals scored on some huge occasions, from UEFA Champions League knockout nights to dramatic Premier League encounters. There is plenty of quality to choose from, too. A stunning volley off the crossbar, a mazy individual run, an overhead kick and a last-minute winner all feature in Group C. The two goals which receive the most votes will advance to the quarter-finals, as we continue to narrow down our 20 Goal of the Season winners along the road to finding the ultimate winner. You can watch all five Group C contenders below, relive each special moment and choose your favourite by voting on the Chelsea Official App, so make sure you have your say on which strikes deserve to progress. Cast your vote for our Ultimate Goal of the Season on the Chelsea Official App here On a huge Champions League night at Stamford Bridge, Essien met a looping ball outside the penalty area with a magnificent left-footed volley, which crashed in off the underside of the crossbar to give us the lead against Barcelona. Ramires showcased the full extent of his skill and dribbling ability against Man City, weaving his way between defenders just outside the penalty area before bearing down on goal and firing beyond Joe Hart to round off a 2-0 victory at the Bridge. One of Hazard’s most memorable moments in Chelsea blue. Picking up possession inside his own half, Eden powered away from the Arsenal midfield, shrugged off Francis Coquelin and continued into the box before calmly beating Petr Cech to complete a sensational solo goal. Giroud produced a spectacular moment in our Champions League last-16 first leg against Atletico, adjusting brilliantly from 12 yards to send an overhead kick beyond Jan Oblak and secure a valuable victory on our way to lifting the Champions League trophy for the second time. Against the club where he had spent the previous season on loan, Gallagher marked his first Chelsea goal in style. First he nutmegged Jean-Philippe Mateta, before curling a brilliant effort into the top corner from outside the box in the 90th minute, to seal a 2-1 victory at Selhurst Park. news.title: Ellie Carpenter on a 'massive rivalry', revenge and a sea of blue
news.body_en: Ellie Carpenter now has enough experience at Chelsea to know that our contests against Arsenal are always high stakes. In the WSL last season - Carpenter's first in blue - we drew at the Emirates Stadium before losing at home to our rivals. Then came a two-legged knockout clash in the Women’s Champions League quarter-final. With the atmosphere at fever pitch in both legs, the Gunners took a 3-1 lead into the decisive leg back in SW6, despite a closely-fought battle. The season before we had overturned a two-goal deficit against Manchester City at the Bridge in the UWCL quarter-final, securing a famous 3-0 victory. The whole stadium believed we could do the same again against Arsenal. A superb performance followed, but Sjoeke Nusken's late goal wasn't enough for us to advance. That’s where Carpenter picks up the story as we prepare to take on Arsenal at the Bridge once more, this time in the Women’s Super League. ‘It's a massive rivalry,’ she tells us. ‘Even before I joined the club, I remember I would always watch Arsenal against Chelsea. It's just one you'd want to put on TV. It’s always a good match, and always a high-tempo game with lots of things happening. It’s probably the biggest rivalry in the league. ‘None of us will ever forget that second leg against Arsenal, because of how well we played and also beating them as well. I guess we still want that bit of revenge for not going through to the semi-final of the Champions League. I'm sure that's in the back of our minds as well. ‘Arsenal are a great team, they have great players, and I'm sure they'll be up for the game. They’ve not been winning their recent matches in the league, so I'm sure they'll be hungry to get more points. It'll be a big game, so we'll have to turn up, and everyone will have to be at their best to win.’ Renee Slegers’ side have scored just twice in their opening three WSL games. After a 1-0 win over Brighton and Hove Albion, and a goalless draw with newly-promoted Crystal Palace, they needed a last-minute goal to grab a point against Manchester United. Yet as Carpenter explains, the team is unconcerned with any previous form, especially as the level of competition in the league is constantly increasing. ‘For us, we just need to focus on ourselves and play the football that we've been playing this season,’ she continued. ‘I think we've had really great performances in all three games. Now it's just about finishing off all the chances we're creating. We just need to keep playing our game plan. ‘Every game is big in the WSL. Right now is probably the strongest the league has ever been. Anyone can win on any given day. Anyone can take points from anyone, and that's what's so good about this league. ‘It's so competitive, and you have to be at your best every weekend to get the three points. That's why I think it's the best league in the world.’ Carpenter has been in top form so far this season. She earned the Player of the Match trophy against Birmingham City, and was also voted Star of the Match for her performance that day by our own supporters. Ahead of one of the biggest tests of the season, the Australian explained why she is revelling in the challenge of playing at the highest level for the Blues. ‘It’s why I wanted to move to England, for sure,’ she says. ‘To play for Chelsea is to play in the best league and to be tested every weekend. Not just against Arsenal, but every weekend it's a test, and you have to bring your best game to get the three points. ‘That’s what I'm enjoying about this league: the expectation and also the pressure to perform. It’s really helped me personally to grow as a footballer on the pitch. ‘I've had a good pre-season with the team, and I guess I'm in a more attacking role these first couple of matches, so it's been nice to get forward and probably more on the attack.’ We have declared the fixture against Arsenal a ‘Blue Day’, meaning there will be special events happening in and around the ground so that our supporters can show their allegiance in a very visual way on Sunday. Answer Ellie's call and get your tickets for Arsenal at the Bridge! Fans are being encouraged to wear Chelsea blue, bring their scarves and wave the flags that will be left on the seats. For those in the West Lower, there will be cards provided to make a mosaic as the teams walk out. And as the derby takes place during a break in men’s fixtures for internationals, it’s the ideal time for all Chelsea fans to show that London is blue. Ellie agrees. ‘It'll be good to see a sea of blue in the stands,’ she says. ‘Hopefully not many red shirts! It'll be nice to see Stamford Bridge full of blue, cheering for us, and hopefully we’ll get a great crowd.’ You can still attend today's huge London derby clash, with kick-off at the Bridge at 4.30pm!

news.title: From the archive: Peter Bonetti on the 1970 FA Cup final
news.body_en: On what would have been his 85th birthday, we look back to when the late, great Peter Bonetti shared his account of one of his greatest moments at Chelsea, our maiden FA Cup triumph in 1970. In the eyes of many, Bonetti - who sadly passed away in 2020 - is regarded as Chelsea's most legendary goalkeeper, and one of the greatest of his incredible 729 games for the Blues was reserved for the biggest of stages. In the FA Cup final of 1969/70, ‘the Cat’ was bright, brave and brilliant across two hours of high-octane, high-stakes football. He made some truly spectacular saves in the first game at Wembley and was our stand-out player as Dave Sexton’s side twice came from behind to force a replay. Up at Old Trafford a fortnight later, with a record TV audience of over 28 million watching at home, Bonetti’s efforts were superhuman as he battled through an early injury to defy Leeds United as our last line of defence. Although it was feline agility and reflexes that earned him his nickname, it was the heart of a lion in Manchester that saw him soldier on through another period of extra time, during which David Webb bundled in that famous winner to ensure the Blues were FA Cup victors for the very first time in our history. Those who watched at the time recall it as one of the most memorable goalkeeping performances in FA Cup final history, while the man who wore the gloves remembers it as the most physical game of his career. ‘They’re two of the most important games, as far as I’m concerned, in Chelsea’s history,’ Bonetti told us in 2010. ‘My memories of the FA Cup final are fantastic and obviously the games were quite exceptional too. ‘It was between two teams that didn’t really like one another and so it was obviously going to be a very physical battle between the two. I’d say that the replay at Old Trafford was the most physical game I ever played in. ‘I wasn’t necessarily referring to the Mick Jones incident where he banged into my knee because that sort of thing can happen – you go up and try to catch a ball and someone challenges you. His knee caught my knee and I don’t think it was deliberate. ‘So I didn’t just mean it was physical because of that, but both teams were so desperate to win because they didn’t like one another at the time. And I must say "at the time" because it’s a bit different today! ‘If the game had been refereed according to the rules and regulations of today, it wouldn’t have lasted! The tackling was wild, you had people kicking each other six foot in the air and trying to kick the ball as someone headed it! ‘But that was the way the game was played in those days, it was very physical. You were out to win, just like nowadays, but it was played in a more aggressive manner, I must admit.’ Bonetti felt it was the Chelsea character that proved the difference between two well-matched teams and speculated on what might have been had his own Herculean effort proved insufficient to keep him on the field after that first-half knee injury. A collision with Leeds centre-forward Jones had done the damage, leaving the Chelsea No1 struggling to even walk properly and requiring a pain-killing injection at half-time. At a time before substitute goalkeepers had been introduced to the game, there was a chance that the eventual match-winner could have had an altogether different role to play. ‘We showed great character over the two games,’ continued Bonetti. ‘I think we were behind three times and got back each time before Webby got the winner. It showed we had great character as a team and a tremendous blend of players. ‘We weren’t surprised when Webby got the goal. He was a great character who was fearless – he’d go up for set-pieces and just throw himself at everything. And he was a very recognised goal scorer too. He scored in the quarter-final and semi-final that year, and I remember him scoring three goals in a Boxing Day match at Ipswich once. He had the eye for a goal, no doubt about it. ‘If my knee injury had kept me out of the game then he’d have been the one to go in goal! If I got injured, he used to go in goal.’ The Cat was voted runner-up in the Footballer of the Year award at the end of that campaign, his FA Cup winners’ medal alongside others in the League Cup, European Cup Winners’ Cup and, of course, the FIFA World Cup. After hanging up his gloves in 1986, it was those medals that ultimately provided most pride to Bonetti. ‘It was the first time the club had ever won the FA Cup and the other thing was that it meant we won medals,' he concluded. ‘You always look back on your career at times when you have won something and there’s so many players who go through their careers without winning anything. So I regard myself as being lucky at having been able to win a couple of things.’ For the supporters who watched him at Stamford Bridge in his prime, it was certainly the Blues who were the lucky ones, for being able to count on Bonetti between the posts during an unbelievable Chelsea career spanning 20 years.

news.title: Ready for the London derby test 💪
Ultimate Goal of the Season | Group C
Internationals: Morgan Rogers features in England defeat
news.body_en: Blues forward Morgan Rogers was a second-half substitute as the Three Lions fell to a 3-2 defeat to world champions Spain at Wembley. It was an entertaining start to England’s Nations League campaign as Lamine Yamal opened the scoring within two minutes under the arch after pouncing on a defensive error, before the Three Lions hit back as Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane both struck to put the hosts into a 2-1 lead. After the break, Alex Baena levelled for the World Cup holders and, with 20 minutes left to play, Rogers was introduced by former Blues manager and current England boss Thomas Tuchel. Although Spain had the final say as Mikel Oyarzabal restored their lead soon after, Rogers looked bright, working angles from both flanks and delivering an impressive cross which was turned behind for a corner. Rogers could be in action once again on Tuesday when England head to Prague to take on Czechia in matchday two of the Nations League, with kick-off set for 7.45pm (UK time).

news.title: Chelsea’s Ultimate Goal of the Season: Group B results
news.body_en: After the next round of voting for Chelsea's Ultimate Goal of the Season competition, the results are in. Ramires and Joao Pedro have secured their place in the quarter-finals... news.title: Chelsea Women trio talk rivalry with Arsenal ahead of Stamford Bridge derby
news.body_en: As we look ahead to a huge London derby with Arsenal at Stamford Bridge on Sunday, we spoke with Blues Lucy Bronze, Lauren James and Sjoeke Nusken about what the rivalry means to them. The trio also discussed their standout moments against the Gunners, and one match in particular sprung to mind. Our 3-1 home victory against Arsenal in March 2024 came from a goal by James and a brace from Nusken. Our No.10 recalled that the kick-off was delayed by 30 minutes that day while the away side – who had forgotten their socks – had to source alternatives from our Megastore. Nusken remembers her unusual goal from that game, while Bronze looks back on a special celebration from Nusken and Mayra Ramirez at the Emirates in October 2024. To conclude, the three players reflect on what it would mean to put a marker down with a victory against our rivals at our new permanent home so early in the campaign. Here's what they had to say... Lucy Bronze: Yeah, it's a lot. Now that I play for Chelsea, I realise how big it is. I've played in a lot of derbies before; Merseyside, Manchester, both in France and Spain as well. I think because both teams are very successful, really top-level teams and fighting for the same things, it's probably one of the most heated rivalries I've played in terms of how close the competition is. Lauren James: It's a huge rivalry, but I played there as well, so I have a lot of respect for the club. It's two great teams going up against each other, so it's always going to be a tough game. I always want to do well, and you always want to do even better against the team you played for. Sjoeke Nusken: It's always a special game against them. It’s always the question: red or blue? You can feel the tension from everyone, every fan. Bronze: I remember when we played them at the Emirates in my first season, because Mayra and Sio did a celebration. There was the second leg of the Champions League last year too, and obviously we won the game, but we lost the tie. It was probably one of the most intense and aggressive performances that we have ever put on. We probably deserved a bit more from the game, but it was just such an intense game to be part of. James: For me, it was when we beat them at the Bridge, and they had to wear our socks. Seeing that moment sticks out the most. Nusken: The game when I scored with my bum, maybe! I actually scored twice, and we won this one at Stamford Bridge as well. Bronze: It’s nice to play a big, top team early in the season, especially as we get to play them at home as well. We perform well at home. It will give us a good gauge of where we are in terms of competing for the league. It’s an exciting game to be part of so early on. James: I don't think the season is decided by one game, especially so early on. But we definitely try to go into each game and show people what we're made of. Nusken: It’s always good to win against Arsenal. It's always a statement. I think especially after last season when we lost to them in the Champions League. This is the next game after that, so it will be a big game for us to win this one. Don't miss our huge London derby clash against Arsenal at Stamford Bridge! Secure your seat now...

news.title: Melvine Malard talks 'the good life' at Chelsea in matchday programme
news.body_en: There’s plenty for everyone in the matchday programme for Sunday’s blockbuster Women's Super League fixture between Chelsea Women and Arsenal at Stamford Bridge. We’ve got an interview with Melvine Malard, who has hit the ground running in Blue, as well as Hannah Hampton’s ‘Firsts & Favs’, a pull-out poster of Veerle Buurman and columns from Sonia Bompastor, Erin Cuthbert and Barbara Charone. In a programme exclusive, Malard says she can now think about 'the good life' as she reflects on a summer in which she made the move from Manchester to London, received a Ballon d’Or nomination and got married as well. She’s also looking forward after getting her first taste of life in a Blues shirt. 'In this team, we have a lot of players that can make so much difference with their quality, speed, vision, and dribbling,' she says. 'For the No9 like me, that’s an amazing thing when you play in this team.' She also discusses head coach Bompastor, with whom she goes way back, and admits she can’t wait to get out there for this massive derby game. 'I think it means a lot in London, it’s a big day in English football – two big teams, with big players, a lot of fans, in a big stadium. I can’t wait because when you play football, you want games like this coming, and I hope when this game comes, we will win!' In addition to all of that, we’ve also got your in-depth head-to-head game preview, all the opposition info and the latest facts and stats, not to mention plenty of puzzles and games to keep everyone occupied before the big kick-off and on the journey home. So be sure to get your copy from the programme sellers around the stadium!

news.title: Trailer 🎥 Millie | A CFCW film
Jordan Henderson: My Football Firsts
news.body_en: Jordan Henderson takes on our quick-fire questions about his early days in football to help you get to know our summer signing a little better. What was the first football match you went to? My first game would have been at Roker Park, to see Sunderland. I can't remember the exact game, but that’s where it would have been, when I was very young. What were your first pair of football boots? I can’t remember what type, but they were probably Nike. What was the first football kit you owned? Probably the Sunderland kit, I definitely would have had a Sunderland shirt when I was very young. I think I can remember having a reversible Barcelona one as well, that was gold on one side. What was the first team you played for? You’re testing my memory! I’m older than everyone else, it was longer ago for me. I can’t remember, sorry. Who was your first room-mate on away trips? I played in the youth team with Martyn Waghorn. That was the youngest, I think, we were youth team age. Who was your first professional game against? In the Premier League it was against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge. I can remember it well because we lost 5-0! We were 3-0 down at half-time, and I came on, so it was not great. But it was a good Chelsea team we were playing against. I think my first-ever match for Sunderland was in a pre-season game against Ajax. Who was your first professional goal against? Professionally, I think it was for Coventry when I was on loan, against Norwich away in the Championship. What was your first emotion when you signed for Chelsea? It was a huge opportunity I couldn’t turn down. I was very excited to get going.

news.title: Internationals: Goal and assist for Acheampong as Lavia makes winning return
news.body_en: Josh Acheampong scored his first goal for England at Under-21 level while Romeo Lavia and Maxence Lacroix opened their UEFA Nations League campaigns with victories. Lavia’s solitary previous international cap had come in March 2023, but his impressive start to the season with Chelsea saw him named in new Belgium manager Mark van Bommel’s first squad. His return to the pitch for his country came off the bench for the final 15 minutes, as he helped Belgium see out a professional but deserved 2-0 win away against Italy, to make a victorious start to the new Nations League campaign. Mark Penders was not involved for Belgium, while Honest Ahanor – who will join Chelsea next year – was an unused substitute for Italy. Lacroix featured at centre-back for the full 90 minutes as Zinedine Zidane made a winning start to life as France manager, beating Turkiye 1-0 in their own Nations League opener. They were made to work hard for their victory though, with chances for both teams before and after Kylian Mbappe’s solitary goal, until a late red card for Turkiye helped Les Blues and Lacroix to hold on to their clean sheet and the three points. Belgium and France will next face each other in the Nations League, in Brussels on Monday evening. Acheampong was named in England Under-21s’ starting line-up alongside fellow Blue Jamie Gittens, as they took on Kazakhstan in qualifying for next year’s UEFA European Under-21 Championship. In an end-to-end match the defender found the bottom corner with a sweet strike to put the Young Lions 2-1 up, having originally fallen behind, but the scores were levelled by half-time. Acheampong played a big part in England retaking the lead after the break, as his cushioned header was volleyed in by his centre-back partner Max Alleyne, before they scored again in added time to secure a 4-2 win. Another victory over Slovakia next Friday would officially book reigning champions England’s place at Euro 2027 with a game to spare. Geovany Quenda was in the Portugal Under-21s side which suffered a narrow defeat away at Bulgaria. He forced an excellent save from the home goalkeeper on three occasions before Portugal took the lead, but was withdrawn in the 88th minute, shortly after Bulgaria had equalised. That meant he was powerless to prevent his team conceding a decisive injury-time goal to lose 2-1. Defeat denied them qualification for the Under-21 Euros on the night, although a home win over Gibraltar on Wednesday would seal Portugal’s spot, regardless of other results. Elsewhere, Freddy Bernal and Chizaram Ezenwata both started for England Under-19s - as did Reggie Walsh, who is spending this season on loan with Wigan Athletic - in their narrow 1-0 friendly win over the Republic of Ireland at St George's Park.

news.title: Key talking points from Sonia Bompastor's pre-Arsenal press conference
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor faced the media at Cobham ahead of our Women's Super League clash with Arsenal at Stamford Bridge, and here are the stand-out talking points from her press conference. We host the Gunners at Stamford Bridge on Sunday afternoon, and if you haven't got your ticket sorted already, you can still purchase yours here. The Blues have won all but one of our six matches so far this season, the anomaly a 1-1 draw with Aston Villa on the opening day of the Women's Super League campaign. Chelsea supporters are being asked to wear blue to make this London derby a 'Blue Day' in the stands and the whole team is looking forward to the clash, as Bompastor explained... 'It's two great teams going against each other. So when you are passionate about football, as a head coach and a player, you want to be involved in those games. 'We are really excited for the game on Sunday. We are playing at home, at Stamford Bridge. We are hoping for our fans to come and support us and hopefully we'll put on a strong performance to have a great afternoon.' 'I think it's important to have players who are able to beat their opponent, especially when you play against a team who are man-marking. 'Alyssa has the technicality and the speed to always beat her opponent one-v-one no matter the situation, whether she's facing forward or whether she's receiving the ball to feet and going beyond the back line. She's a player who loves to play with freedom because she has a lot of instinct and it's great to have a player like her. 'She can make a lot of difference on the pitch, so that's really important as well, especially when you play in big games.' 'I think fine margins will decide the game for sure and the details are really important. Both teams will have to be really strong in the defensive aspects not to concede, but also to create and be clinical to score the opportunities we make in the game. 'It's a massive fixture not only for the club and the players, but also for the fans. We want to play from the first minute until the end of the game and we will give our all to make sure we bring the fans along with us. The best way is to score and to embrace the game. So we'll try to do that.' 'I think that was the first time in the season where we faced a team with a direct style of football. The only thing they wanted to do is to play long balls behind the back line, then fight for the first and the second ball. 'So it was good for us to be in that position. And even against a team who played direct, I don't think we conceded many opportunities. I think we were strong in the duels and also we dealt well with the transitions. 'But also we faced a team who were man-marking everywhere on the pitch. We spoke a lot about finding solutions when you play a team who are doing that in terms of the spaces and the different movements you need to create the space. 'It was really positive to be going into these next two games having faced a team who were causing us some challenges. So it's good to approach Sunday's game having had this one in the bag.' 'I think for me, the most important thing – as I told my players – it's not always about the system, but instead it's about the way we animate the system. 'But we don't change our main principles and our philosophy no matter what system we are playing. So for me, I have players smart enough to know and to recognise the positions they need to play and what they need to do in every position they are playing in, and they are adaptable with that, so it's good.' Don't miss our huge London derby clash against Arsenal at Stamford Bridge! Secure your seat now...

news.title: Sonia Bompastor gives fitness updates on Lauren James and Keira Walsh
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor delivered a team news update on a key Chelsea quartet ahead of our London derby with Arsenal on Sunday afternoon. The Blues face a big test this weekend as we go up against rivals Arsenal, and Bompastor gave the latest on who she will have available to face the Gunners. There remains a doubt over whether two of our key players will be fit to start at Stamford Bridge on Sunday. Lauren James missed Wednesday evening's win over Austria Vienna with what the head coach described as a small knock, while Keira Walsh started in midweek but was substituted 20 minutes in, after feeling some pain in her calf. 'It's probably one of the first times I'm not in a position to share a lot with you,' explained Bompastor. 'Because we played two days ago, and we still have a training session tomorrow. 'I need to meet with my performance staff to assess all the players and I'll probably have more information tomorrow before the game.' There was some good news about another key duo from the Friday afternoon press conference. After a pre-planned substitution at half-time against Austria Vienna, Melvine Malard came through unscathed and will be available for selection on Sunday. Our head coach explained some of the striker's key attributes. 'Melvine was training this morning, so she's in a good place,' Bompastor continued. 'She's in contention for the game on Sunday. It was the plan for her to play 45 minutes. She's still building from pre-season. 'I think she's a player who is really confident now. She's the No9 for the French national team, but she also came into our environment with a lot of confidence from last season and the good season she had with Man United. 'She's really technical and has a lot of speed in the attacking line, so she's a threat for any team, and I think it's good to have her in our squad. So hopefully she'll have a good game on Sunday if she's starting or coming on.' Naomi Girma is also returning to fitness and was an unused substitute in Wednesday night's Women's Champions League win. Bompastor explained where the defender is up to in terms of her availability. 'Nay is training fully right now with the squad,' said the head coach. 'I think in the game on Wednesday, it was not always easy to bring defenders on, especially in the last 10 minutes where the balls were coming and they were playing direct football. 'But she's doing good. She's training fully. I think probably what we need to get from Nay is being consistently on the pitch, but we are all around her trying to support her to be able to achieve that. 'It's great to have a player with her mentality. She's a hard worker and she brings a lot of quality. So if she's able to get minutes again and stay consistently on the pitch, it will be great news.' Internationals: Estevao denied goal on Brazil return
news.body_en: Estevao Willian made his return to Brazil’s starting line-up and was close to marking it by netting a decisive goal, but had to settle for a draw after his strike was ruled out. The Chelsea winger was recalled by the Selecao for this international window, which they begin with back-to-back friendlies away against Australia. Joao Pedro had also been named in their squad, but was later withdrawn. Estevao went straight into Carlo Ancelotti’s line-up for the first of those friendlies down under, making his first start for his country since scoring in a 1-1 draw with Tunisia last November. It was nearly a similar story in this match, when Estevao thought he had given his team the lead in first-half stoppage time by firing into the bottom-left corner. However, VAR intervened and disallowed the goal for a foul by Bruno Guimaraes in the build-up. Instead it was the hosts Australia who took the lead through a Nestory Irankunda free-kick after the break, despite Brazil having the better of the possession. Estevao was withdrawn with 15 minutes remaining, but Brazil managed to salvage a draw with virtually the last kick of the game, when Rayan headed in a Raphinha corner in the fifth minute of added time. After that 1-1 draw, Brazil and Australia will meet again in Sydney on Tuesday, with kick-off at 11am UK time.

news.body_en: Joao Pedro has been named on the shortlist for the September Premier League Creative Moment of the Month award for his brilliant piece of skill against Hull City. A strong start to the 2026/27 season has already seen our Brazilian striker named as the Premier League Player of the Month in August, and he has now been nominated for a second Premier League award in as many months. Vote for Joao Pedro to win Premier League Creative Moment of the Month It came from one particular passage of play in the draw with Hull, when the Blues were pushing for a winning goal after Joao Pedro had netted our equaliser, and he demonstrated why he has been such a handful for defences during the early stages of this season. First he fooled everyone with a clever dummy to allow Reece James’ pass to run through to Danny Welbeck, then seconds later found his fellow striker again, showing great vision and technique to redirect Cole Palmer’s ball with a back-heeled flick. Voting for the September Premier League Creative Moment of the Month is open now, and you can cast your vote for Joao Pedro to receive the award here until the poll closes at midday on Monday 28 September. The winner will be announced at 1pm on Thursday 1 October. The Blues forward is one of five nominated players on the award’s September shortlist, alongside Martin Zubimendi (Arsenal), Emiliano Buendia (Aston Villa), Abdul Fatawu (Ipswich Town) and Liam Delap (Nottingham Forest).

news.title: Watson and Ezenwata up for PL2 award
news.body_en: Cobham Next Gen midfielder Reggie Watson and attacker Chizaram Ezenwata have both been shortlisted for September’s Premier League 2 Player of the Month award. 16-year-old Watson has been in superb form this month, scoring three goals in two PL2 matches. He netted a brace against Arsenal, leading Cobham Next Gen to a statement 4-1 win. First, he converted from the penalty spot before wrapping a free-kick into the far corner. Watson made an impact against Fulham, too, scoring the Blues’ second goal with a low drive into the bottom corner. That finish took his goal tally this season up to five in PL2. The mature midfielder has now featured on the scoresheet in each of CNG’s league matches this season, while at the beginning of the month, Watson made his senior debut, starting in midfield in our 6-3 win over Leeds United in the third round of the Carabao Cup. Blues striker Ezenwata has also been nominated for this month’s award having started the 2026/27 campaign promisingly. The 18-year-old scored the winner in CNG’s 5-4 win over West Ham, and netted in the win against Arsenal at the start of the month. Ezenwata then showcased his playmaking ability by claiming two assists to complete the 3-1 comeback win against West London rivals Fulham. He also came close to scoring his third league goal of the season in that match, striking the crossbar in the first half with an emphatic left-footed effort. Leo Black, who is currently on trial at Chelsea, also features in the shortlist following some impressive displays, including goals scored against Arsenal and Fulham. Watson’s and Ezenwata’s performances have earned them nominations for September’s Premier League 2 Player of the Month award, alongside Leo Black (Chelsea trialist), Will Wright (Liverpool), Cruz Ibeh (Middlebrough), Harvey Vincent (Leeds United), Charlie Dinsdale (Sunderland) and Tyrese Hall (Tottenham Hotspur). The winner of this month’s award will be announced on Friday 2 October.

news.title: Chelsea Women vs Arsenal: How to watch, kick-off time, live stream info
news.body_en: Chelsea Women host Arsenal in the Women's Super League on Sunday afternoon, in what promises to be an enthralling London derby. Two of women's football's biggest sides go head-to-head on Sunday as we take on the Gunners at Stamford Bridge. After our opening day draw against Aston Villa, we have gone on to record a 5-0 victory away at Manchester United and a 2-0 home win against Birmingham City last weekend. Meanwhile, Arsenal won 1-0 against Brighton & Hove Albion on the opening day, but have struggled in their last two league fixtures. A 0-0 draw at home to Crystal Palace was followed up with a 1-1 stalemate against Man United, as a 95th-minute goal from Smilla Holmberg rescued a point. Here is everything you need to know about how to watch Chelsea Women against Arsenal, including kick-off time and how to follow the action on official Chelsea channels. Chelsea Women's game against Arsenal takes place on Sunday 27 September 2026 at Stamford Bridge, with kick-off scheduled for 4.30pm UK time. The best way to experience the unique atmosphere at the London derby is by coming to the Bridge in person. Tickets for the game are available here. There are a number of special initiatives planned for the day, as supporters are encouraged to make it a 'Blue Day' on Sunday, and you can find out more about that here. If you are unable to join us, then you can watch the match live on Sky One, Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Premier League. As always, team news, live updates and match coverage will be provided in our Chelsea Women vs Arsenal Match Centre on the Chelsea Official App and Chelsea website. You can also follow along via Chelsea Women’s social media channels on X, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok. This Sunday’s game at Stamford Bridge is matchday four in this season’s WSL and is between the sides third and sixth in the table. Chelsea have two points more than Arsenal and trail leaders Manchester City by two points. Chelsea (11 games) and Arsenal (20 games) are on the two longest unbeaten runs in the WSL currently. Since the start of Chelsea’s run on matchday 15 last term (7 February onwards), the Blues average the most points per game in the top flight (2.64), ahead of the Gunners (2.50). Chelsea are unbeaten in each of our past 45 WSL matches when leading at any stage (W38 D7), the longest run in the competition’s history. Arsenal, meanwhile, are unbeaten in their last 42 when ahead (W38 D4), one off their own record run of 43 set between August 2016 and September 2019. This will be the 10th meeting between Chelsea and Arsenal in all competitions since the 2023/24 season, with both teams picking up four wins apiece in that time (with one draw). Arsenal were 2-0 victors in the league at Stamford Bridge against us last season, but not since the first three WSL campaigns (between 2011 and 2013) have they won consecutive WSL away matches versus the Blues. The WSL match at the Emirates last campaign ended 1-1, with Alyssa Thompson putting the Blues ahead early on followed by a late Alessia Russo equaliser. Last season, Chelsea also played Arsenal in the Champions League quarter-finals, exiting 3-2 on aggregate. Lauren James scored in a 3-1 first-leg defeat away and Sjoeke Nusken netted the only goal late on at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea (13 wins) and Arsenal (10 wins) is the most played fixture in WSL history (31 meetings including the 2017 Spring Series).

news.title: Chelsea's Ultimate Goal of the Season: Group B vote
news.body_en: Our search for Chelsea’s Ultimate Goal of the Season continues and Group B has a distinctly Brazilian flavour. After Group A got the competition under way, five more Goal of the Season winners now go head-to-head for two places in the quarter-finals. This time, every contender was scored by a Brazilian Blue, with Juliano Belletti, Ramires, Oscar, Willian and Joao Pedro providing the five moments for you to choose between. There are an array of different goals, with a long-range thunderbolt, an unforgettable chip on one of the biggest nights in our history, a moment of individual brilliance, a wonderful team move and an overhead kick. As with Group A, the two goals which receive the most votes will advance to the quarter-finals, as our field of 20 previous winners is gradually narrowed down on the way to crowning the Ultimate Goal of the Season. The decision over which Brazilian beauties make it through is in your hands. You can watch all five Group B contenders below, relive some memorable moments and pick the two goals you want to see progress by voting over on the Chelsea Official App. Cast your vote for our Ultimate Goal of the Season on the Chelsea Official App here Tottenham afforded Belletti acres of space as he advanced from well inside his own half and the Brazilian made them pay in spectacular fashion, unleashing a thunderous drive from 35 yards, which flew into the top corner at the Shed End. On an unforgettable Champions League night at the Nou Camp, Ramires raced on to Frank Lampard’s perfectly weighted pass and produced an audacious first-time chip over Victor Valdes to put us ahead in the tie on away goals. We of course went on to win our first Champions League that year, making this goal all the more memorable. On his first Chelsea start, Oscar announced himself in style. With his back to goal on the edge of the box, he took a fantastic touch from Ashley Cole's pass, spinning away from two Juventus players before curling a magnificent effort beyond Gianluigi Buffon and into the top corner. A goal to give the word teamwork a new meaning. Willian exchanged a series of quick passes with Eden Hazard and Michy Batshuayi, in the process slicing through the Brighton defence, before firing home from the edge of the penalty area. Joao Pedro brought up the 20th goal of his debut Chelsea season in spectacular style, controlling Marc Cucurella’s header on his chest before producing an acrobatic overhead kick, which flew beyond Matz Sels and into the far corner. news.title: Internationals: Neto helps Portugal to winning start
news.body_en: Pedro Neto helped Portugal begin their Nations League campaign with a 1-0 victory over Wales. Neto started for Portugal at the Estadio Jose Alvalade in Lisbon as new head coach Jorge Jesus marked his first match in charge with three points. It was former Blue Joao Felix who broke the deadlock midway through the first half. His effort from outside the penalty area took a deflection off Ben Davies to beat Wales goalkeeper Danny Ward, and ultimately proved enough to settle the contest. Portugal were more dominant than the scoreline suggested, having 23 shots at goal to Wales' five and Neto created an opening which saw a Ronaldo effort easily saved by Ward. The former Real Madrid and Manchester United man had the ball in the back of the net early in the second half but the goal was ruled out for offside. Elsewhere, Jorrel Hato remained on the bench as the Netherlands left it late to secure a 1-1 draw with Germany in Amsterdam. Felix Nmecha put the visitors ahead after 32 minutes, but Cody Gakpo struck in the second minute of stoppage time to earn the hosts a point in their Nations League opener. Both nations are back in action on Sunday, with Hato’s Netherlands travelling to Serbia before Neto and Portugal take on Norway in Oslo.
